diagnosis: I calibrated the model with DDS on NSE over 1971-1997, after a one-year warm-up. That took 3000 runs, followed by a 2500-run refinement with a different random seed. The calibration NSE is 0.839 (KGE 0.80, r 0.92), but the model overestimates total flow by about 10% (PBIAS +10%). It most likely overpredicts dry-season baseflow and smaller events, probably because of urban water abstraction or management and the one reservoir. Very sharp flood peaks are also likely underestimated: the highest simulated flow is about 30 mm/d against an observed 33.5 mm/d. Snow plays a minor role (2.6% of precipitation falls as snow). Because of that, the snow parameters are poorly constrained, and CFR and CWH ended up at their lower bound of 0. The key parameters are FC≈180 mm, LP≈0.86, BETA≈2.1, K1≈0.35, K2≈0.055, PERC≈1.4, UZL≈8.7 and MAXBAS≈2.8. The second run with a different seed returned the same NSE and nearly the same values, so I'm moderately to highly confident in the soil and response parameters. I did not run a split-sample validation. Even so, I'd expect an NSE of roughly 0.78-0.83 in the 1998-2008 period, as long as the catchment's management and climate stay similar.
